verdict.rationale: The SDK's own docs show it can pause a run and later resume from the same RunState, and it also offers session memory for conversation history and resumable sandbox sessions. That is a first-party state-resume mechanism, but it is only documented for human-in-the-loop approval interruptions. Nothing shows arbitrary checkpointing or recovery after a crash or restart. Durable execution via Temporal (comm-3) is an external integration, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: documented checkpointing at arbitrary points, evidence that RunState survives a process crash or restart, documented serialization and persistence of run state, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can checkpoint agent state so a run can resume exactly where it left off after a crash or restart

citations.quote: When a tool call requires approval, the SDK pauses the run, returns `interruptions`, and lets you resume later from the same `RunState`.
Sandbox agents support manifest-defined files, sandbox client selection, and resumable sandbox sessions.
The Agents SDK provides built-in session memory to automatically maintain conversation history across multiple agent runs
